events.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small Next.js app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

events.content:
The app is done and verified working. Run it with `npm run dev` (or `npm run build && npm start`) and open http://localhost:3000.

## What you get

**Home page (`/`)** shows two lists, "Currently reading" and "Finished", plus an "Add a book" form (title, author, optional notes). Each book in the reading list has a "Mark finished" button. Adding a book takes you straight to its page.

**Book page (`/books/<id>`)** shows the title, author, notes, and either a "Mark finished" button or a "Finished on <date>" badge. There's a collapsed "Edit notes" section so you can add to your notes while reading. The URL is stable and shareable, and the page sets a `<title>` of "Title by Author" so links preview sensibly. Unknown IDs get a 404 page.

**Storage** is `data/books.json` in the project root, created automatically on the first add. Writes go through a temp file and rename so a crash can't leave a half-written file, and concurrent submissions are serialized so they can't overwrite each other. I gitignored `data/books.json` so your reading list doesn't end up in commits.

## How it's built

- Next.js 16 App Router with Server Components; reading the file happens on the server at request time.
- Adding, finishing, and editing notes are Server Actions (`lib/actions.ts`), so the forms work even without JavaScript. The add form is the only client component, just to display the "title and author required" error.
- `lib/books.ts` is the whole storage layer (~100 lines). Plain CSS in `app/globals.css`, no UI libraries.
- Six vitest tests in `lib/books.test.ts` cover the storage module (`npm test`), including the concurrent-add case.

## Verification

I built the production bundle (clean, no warnings), started the server, and drove the actual forms over HTTP: added a book, confirmed it appeared under "Currently reading" and on its own page with notes, confirmed the validation error for a missing author, marked it finished and saw it move to the "Finished" list, edited its notes, and got a 404 for a bogus ID. I then killed and restarted the server and the book was still there. Test data was removed afterwards.

Nothing is committed yet; the new files are sitting in the working tree on `master`.
